transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: How are you? I'm good. What about you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, doctor. I'm good.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: What happened? Tell me. What is your problem?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm having difficulty in breathing, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And also I'm having fever from yesterday 6:00 PM, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Okay, did you check your temperature?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No doctor. Yes doctor, I have checked it. It is around 101 degrees fever.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Apart from fever, do you have cough or cold?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Dry cough. Cold is cold is very mild, but throat irritation, I have throat irritation also.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Sore throat or did you find difficulty in swallow by swallowing or pain?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Slight pain, doctor. Water taagithe ok undi, but food tine tapudu little discomfort undi.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Any breathing difficulty, chest pain?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No doctor, breathing normal ga undi, chest pain ledu.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Headache ledha dizziness unda?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Headache undi. Morning nunchi weakness kuda feel avtunnanu.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Vomitings, loose motions or stomach pain emyna?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No doctor, avemi levu.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Appetite ela undi? Properly tintunara?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, good. Good doctor. Appetite is good.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Water, did you take plenty of water?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Not much doctor. Throat because of throat irritation, I'm taking very less water.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Did you travel?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No doctor. Yes doctor, I had travel yesterday night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: On basis of work.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Okay, done. Temperature is 100 degrees Celsius. Pulse is slightly high because of fever. Blood pressure is normal. Oxygen saturation is 98%, which is good.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Please open your mouth, let me examine your throat. Your throat is mildly red. I can hear you hear a slight dry cough. At present, it looks like a viral upper respiratory infection. Most viral fevers improve within 3 days to 5 days. Antibiotics avasarama doctor? Ledhu, right now you don't need antibiotics. Viral infections usually don't require antibiotics unless there is evidence of bacterial infection, okay? I'll prescribe paracetamol for fever, cough cough syrup for dry cough, and vitamin supplements. Drink plenty of water, okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah doctor.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: If you develop breathing difficulty, severe chest pain, continuous vomiting, confusion, or oxygen level drops below 94%, visit the hospital immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay doctor, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Take the medicines on time. Drink at least 2 to 3 liters of fluids and get enough sleep.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay doctor, thank you. I'll follow this.

summary.chief_complaint: Fever, dry cough, throat irritation, and pain when swallowing.
summary.consultation_overview: Patient presented with fever, dry cough, mild cold, throat irritation, slight pain on swallowing food, headache, and weakness since yesterday evening. On examination, the doctor noted mild throat redness and dry cough, diagnosing a viral upper respiratory infection. Symptomatic medications and fluid intake were recommended.
summary.history_of_present_illness: Patient experienced fever starting yesterday at 6:00 PM, measuring around 101°F at home. Reports dry cough, mild cold, throat irritation, slight pain when eating food, headache, and weakness since morning. Breathing is currently normal, with no chest pain, vomiting, loose motions, or stomach pain. Patient traveled last night for work and has been drinking less water due to throat irritation.
examination_findings: Slight dry cough present on examination
summary.treatment_plan: Prescribed paracetamol for fever, cough syrup for dry cough, and vitamin supplements. Recommended drinking 2-3 liters of fluids daily, taking medicines on time, and getting enough sleep.
advice: Drink at least 2 to 3 liters of fluids daily
summary.follow_up: Visit the hospital immediately if breathing difficulty, severe chest pain, continuous vomiting, confusion, or oxygen saturation below 94% develops.
summary.doctor_notes: Antibiotics are not needed at present as viral infections do not require antibiotics unless there is evidence of a bacterial infection.
